punchline: A bagel seller lost about a tenth of his bagels to customers but almost never lost the box that held the money.
thirty_sec: Paul Feldman quit a career as a government economist to sell bagels on the honor system. He left a box of bagels and a cash box in office kitchens and came back later for the money. At first he expected 95 percent payment, then learned to call 90 percent honest. His records showed smaller offices paying better, and a drop just before Christmas. He lost about one cash box a year out of thousands, though people ate his bagels for free.
